title: Azt Mondta, Hogy...: Reporting What Someone Said

sections.title: Pointing forward to what was said
sections.content: To report what someone said, Hungarian points forward with azt ("that", the accusative of az) before mondta ("said it") — Azt mondta, hogy... literally means "He/she said IT, that...". mondta is definite because azt itself is the definite, specific thing being said; everything after hogy fills in what that "it" actually was, in its own normal word order and tense. mond is a fully regular verb — mondtam, mondtad, mondta — so nothing about the shape of the sentence is new, only the pattern.

sections.title: azt ..., hogy ...
rows: Azt mondta, hogy vicces volt a történet.
She said (that) the story was funny.

items.spanish: Petra azt mondta, hogy nagyon vicces volt a történet.
items.english: Petra said that the story was very funny.

items.spanish: Azt mondtam Károlynak, hogy elveszítettem a kulcsomat.
items.english: I told Károly that I'd lost my key.
What did Tamás say about the story?

sections.content: azt mondta is how you REPORT speech; it's different from just asking Mit mondott? ("What did he/she say?") — a question needs no azt, because there's no specific "it" being pointed at yet.
